item.title: The Complete Drawer Slides Buying Guide for Nigeria (2026)
item.description:
The Complete Drawer Slides Buying Guide for Nigeria

I’ve been exporting hardware to Africa for over a decade, and if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s this: nobody thinks about drawer slides until the drawer jams.

And by then, it’s too late.

I remember sitting in a furniture workshop in Mushin, Lagos, back in 2018. A master carpenter named Chidi had just finished a beautiful set of bedroom wardrobes for a client in VI. The woodwork was flawless — solid iroko, hand-finished joinery, the kind of craftsmanship you’d pay a premium for anywhere in the world. But when we pulled open one of the drawers, it screeched like a dying cat, wobbled side to side, and then stopped halfway. Chidi turned to me with a look I’ve seen a hundred times since. “Na this slide be the problem,” he said. “I buy cheap one from Balogun.”

item.title: Why Hardware Rusts Fast in Nigeria (And How to Prevent It)
item.description:
If you’ve noticed door handles, hinges, and locks rusting within months of installation in Nigeria, you’re not alone. This is one of the most common complaints we hear from customers in Lagos, Port Harcourt, and other coastal cities.

The good news? Most of these failures are preventable. Here’s the practical guide based on 10 years of supplying hardware to the Nigerian market.

Why Rust Happens Faster in Nigeria

1. Coastal humidity

Lagos and Port Harcourt have humidity levels above 80% for most of the year. This creates the perfect environment for electrochemical corrosion.

item.title: Certifications That Matter (And Ones That Don't) — From 10 Years of Nigerian Customs Nightmares
